audit: Third Falling Sky / Liberty or Death comparison audit

grouping.note: Counts repair groups, not every symptom, parameter, profile or witness. FE3-01 has two internal metadata sinks; BE3-01 includes two Consuetudine clauses; XC3-01 spans existing Colony consumers.

suggested_batches.theme: Protect authored input and board integrity
Correct action boundaries and seasonal calculations
Unify dynamic Tribe and persistent effect handling

limits: Focused adversarial audit, not an exhaustive proof of rules correctness. Existing tests and mixed-seat validation do not generate all these boundary cases.
Controlled initialized boards are distinguished from full file-session journeys in partition evidence. Pool and structure checks do not establish every rule effect.
Entreat witness intentionally ends with a structural error; all other final witness boards preserve the asserted inventory and structural invariants.

Dispersed Colony scoring uses an explicitly assigned legal marker because the existing Seize bug blocks that path. Some Colony operations use validated production primitives rather than a full saved frontend journey.
Journal corruption substitutes Pass for the accepted Recruit; replay consistently reproduces the substituted action, not a replay exception.
Lost Eagle post-Interlude retention is static corroboration only. Confirmed expiry witness uses first Pax forced Senate.
Known Circumvallation persistence work, two unresolved source questions and earlier closed findings are excluded. Provisional rulings are retained.
Liberty or Death provides engineering comparisons only. All game-rule conclusions use supplied Falling Sky references and adopted project decisions.

findings.title: Authored turn metadata can override Eligibility and accepted decisions during resume
findings.expected: Only player-owned action fields may influence a submitted turn. An ordinary Recruit makes its executor Ineligible. A pause and resume must preserve the exact accepted Command and its engine-owned journal identity.
findings.observed: validate_response returns an arbitrary top-level turn object unchanged. resolve_card_turn stores that object as action history, where free_action is trusted for Eligibility. SeatSession.ask also merges the object over its freshly constructed journal entry, allowing assistant_response to replace the accepted response that will be replayed on resume.

subcases.name: unauthorized_free_action
subcases.setup: Ordinary llm_seat init/play/submit, The Great Revolt, Romans, seed 46. Submit a one-Auxilia Recruit in Provincia as the first action on card 16.
subcases.control: Without extra metadata, one Auxilia is placed and Romans become Ineligible when card 16 completes.
subcases.defect: With top-level free_action=true, the same ordinary Recruit places the same Auxilia but Romans become Eligible at completion of card 16.
subcases.observation_note: The script wraps adjust_eligibility with an observation-only recorder that calls the original unchanged implementation before recording. The next human turn happens to be card 17 in both runs because other factions take both action slots on intervening card 45. The finding is the directly observed erroneous Eligibility state, not a claimed extra action in this seed.

subcases.name: journal_response_collision
subcases.setup: Same ordinary initialized session and valid Recruit, but add top-level assistant_response={action:pass}. Submit explicit use_default responses for the normal reactive requests.
subcases.control: The accepted Recruit adds one Auxilia, 6 to 7 in Provincia. The next human turn is card 17. The original action is recorded and exact replay verifies.
subcases.defect: The initial Recruit is accepted, but its normal pause and resume reads the caller-overwritten journal assistant_response and executes Pass instead. Provincia remains at 6 Auxilia. End-card16 action is Pass, next human turn is card45, and the durable log still presents action=command with the Recruit player_action while assistant_response={action:pass}. Replay verifies the substituted behavior because it trusts that altered journal.

findings.comparison_pattern: Separate user choices from engine-owned state and history, and verify the action actually executed. Liberty or Death's engine constructs its turn-log fields explicitly and maintains eligibility exceptions through state helpers.
findings.relationship_to_prior_findings: New boundary within the same general authored-input class as FE2-01/FE2-02 and XC2-01. Those repairs bind inner plan type/current card and command scope; they do not reserve top-level execution/journal metadata. No earlier closed finding or Circumvallation follow-up is recounted. Both effects are conservatively grouped because they share arbitrary top-level metadata admission.
findings.repair_scope: Define and enforce the supported turn-response envelope at durable and raw human turn boundaries; keep free-action/eligibility authority engine-owned; build protected journal metadata without allowing authored fields to overwrite it. Preserve legal existing turn fields and explicitly authorized compatibility records.
findings.regression_gate: Both invalid submissions should remain pending without board/RNG/history mutation. Cover ordinary Command, Event and Pass envelopes, direct human callbacks as appropriate, corrected retry, normal reactive pause/resume, save/load and replay; ensure genuine Event eligibility exceptions remain legal.

findings.title: Entreat can target a Citadel City and remove a different Tribe’s Ally disc
findings.expected: Entreat may replace an Allied Tribe disc, not a Citadel. Check that the named Tribe is backed by an actual eligible Ally disc before removing anything.
findings.observed: A prepared census/structurally valid Great Revolt position has a Belgic Citadel at Sequani and a Belgic Ally at Helvetii. Arverni Entreat naming Sequani is accepted. findings.title: Authored ordinary Battle plans can grant themselves Event-only combat powers
findings.expected: Only trusted Event resolution may grant modified Battle strength, combined forces, prohibited Retreat or forced Retreat. Ordinary player plan fields cannot confer those powers.
findings.observed: Without active Event modifiers, durable validation accepts details.warband_full_loss, allied_factions, no_retreat and force_retreat. Four Aedui Warbands kill two of eight Germans normally, four with full-loss flag, and six with allied_factions=[Aedui,Aedui]. A declared refusal to Retreat is overridden by force_retreat, removing all five opposing Arverni Warbands; no_retreat suppresses the defender’s Retreat question entirely. All resulting positions pass census and structure.

findings.rule: Reference Documents/Card Reference 53, lines 528–534; Chapter 5 §5.1.1; Chapter 4 §4.2.2
findings.rule_excerpt: Battling with Ambush regardless of the numbers of Hidden enemies
findings.expected: Four German Warbands in Pictones must Ambush five Hidden Aedui Warbands, inflicting two Losses and removing two Warbands. No German Rally placement is available in Pictones and no Raid occurs because Resources are zero. Separately, The Scouted German Warband in Pictones loses its marker and remains Revealed.

findings.title: Seize treats Razed Cities as Subdued and replaces their permanent marker
findings.expected: A City Razed by Sacking is Dispersed for Seize, yields no ordinary Forage, cannot be Dispersed again, and retains its Razed marker through Spring.
findings.observed: An accepted Sacking Event Razes Roman-controlled Alesia. Seize's menu offers Mandubii for dispersal and its Forage calculator returns 4 instead of 2. A full authored Seize is accepted, earns 8, and changes Razed to ordinary Dispersed. Two Spring phases then clear the status, whereas a matched control remains Razed. State and structural validation report no errors throughout.

rules.quote: Unshaded marker is the equivalent of a Dispersed marker for all purposes except it is not removed in Spring

comparison.pattern: Trace a persistent marker from its setter through later action and seasonal observation points, including alternate representations of the same rule concept.
